# Driftline

> Driftline is a GitHub Action and CLI that finds OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, xAI, Cohere, DeepSeek and Groq model IDs (and Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI and Azure's own dates) in a codebase, warns before those models are retired, and (Pro) runs your real prompts on the current and the replacement model to show what changes. It runs in your own CI with your own API keys; there is no Driftline server.

- Free scan: `npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .` in any repository (no install, no key). Add `--json` for machine-readable output. Exit code 1 = a retired model is used in code.
- GitHub Action: `uses: AI-Driftline/driftline@v0` (Marketplace: "Driftline AI Model Check"). Annotates the file and line, writes a job summary, can open one self-updating issue and fail the build.
- Pro: drift tests on your prompts. $19/month or $190/year, one key covers up to 3 GitHub accounts or organizations.
- Tracks 257 model IDs (checked 2026-11-13), including Bedrock, Vertex and OpenRouter spellings and Claude short names.
- License: Elastic License 2.0 (source available). Contact: hello@aidriftline.com

## Retirement data

- [All retirement dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/): every tracked model with date, replacement and source
- [models.json](https://aidriftline.com/models.json): the same data as JSON (fields: id, provider, retires, qualifier exact|earliest|not-before, replacement, kind, routes)
- Per model: https://aidriftline.com/models/<model-id>/ (for example https://aidriftline.com/models/gemini-2.5-pro/)
- [RSS feed](https://aidriftline.com/feed.xml) and [calendar](https://aidriftline.com/retirements.ics) of retirement dates
- [DeepSeek dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/deepseek/): 4 model IDs from DeepSeek's own announcements (no deprecation page; checked daily); retired names are redirected to a newer model (routes). In models.json: `platforms.deepseek.models`.
- [Groq dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/groq/): 30 model IDs from Groq's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours). In models.json: `platforms.groq.models`.
- [Mistral AI dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/mistral/): 47 model IDs from Mistral AI's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours). In models.json: `platforms.mistral.models`.
- [xAI dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/xai/): 9 model IDs from xAI's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours); retired names are redirected to a newer model (routes). In models.json: `platforms.xai.models`.
- [Cohere dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/cohere/): 11 model IDs from Cohere's own deprecation page (checked every 6 hours). In models.json: `platforms.cohere.models`.
- [Azure dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/azure/): 149 Azure OpenAI and Foundry models with Azure's own retirement date per model version, read from Microsoft's schedule every 6 hours. They differ from OpenAI's in both directions (o3: Azure 19 Nov 2026, OpenAI 11 Dec 2026). Azure plans an end date for current models too (lifecycle GA/Preview). In models.json: `platforms.azure.models` (id, maker, retires = earliest version, versions[] with version, lifecycle, retires, replacement).
- [Google Vertex AI dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/vertex/): 64 Vertex model IDs (Gemini, Imagen, Veo, embeddings, Claude, open models ending in -maas) with Vertex's own retirement dates, read from Google Cloud's pages every 6 hours. Vertex uses the Gemini API's model names but its dates often differ (gemini-2.5-pro: retired on Vertex 20 Oct 2026, routed on the Gemini API 1 Dec 2026). In models.json: `platforms.vertex.models`.
- [Amazon Bedrock dates](https://aidriftline.com/models/bedrock/): 56 Bedrock model IDs (Claude, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Cohere and more) with Bedrock's own end-of-life dates per region, read from AWS's page every 6 hours. They often differ from the model maker's dates; for Bedrock calls only Bedrock's apply. In models.json: `platforms.bedrock.models` (id, maker, retires = earliest region, regions[], extended).
- Free email alerts: sign up on any model page for emails 30 days and 7 days before, on the day, and when a date or replacement changes
- How it stays current: a script compares every entry with the official deprecation pages every 6 hours, and an AI check following written rules updates the registry daily or right away when the script finds a difference. Until then, affected models carry `under_review` in models.json and say "under review" on their pages; alerts for them wait.

## For AI coding agents

- [Agent guide](https://aidriftline.com/agents/): how to check model IDs before you write or keep them, and a snippet for AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
- MCP server: `claude mcp add driftline -- npx -y @aidriftline/driftline mcp` (tools: check_models, scan_project, upcoming_retirements)
- Rule of thumb: before adding or keeping an OpenAI, Anthropic or Google model ID, look it up. Do not introduce an ID whose status is retired, or whose date is within 90 days, without telling the user.
